ratings_why.fun: Champion, Proud and Duel wins braid so one Proud Champion is fed by nearly every card, and Chronicler's 4-units-at-dawn against Elder's few-at-dusk makes each turn a real puzzle.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because empty slots are the resource: on a board where gaps never close, you play by leaving holes in a chequerboard, which no current tribe or generic auto-battler does.

verdict_why: One wording fix on Dame Reisig; otherwise the combos are in a good spot and more change would only make it different.

points.text: Dame Reisig says the Champion is your biggest unit of any tribe, but Champion says Hens are never Champion. Say whether a grown Hen, or Reisig herself, can be crowned.
The Chronicler only crosses out the smallest unit, so the build's grown Konrad is rarely the one taken. Letting a Proud unit be chosen instead would make feeding Konrad a deliberate play.
Pennon-Squire is the only Duel-giver outside Ottokar; if it gave Duel to a unit across a gap (making it Proud-friendly), it would tie the Duel and Proud builds at Tier 2.
The reading-order puzzle (Warden's Shield, Gottfried's multiplier and Herald's Duels all at Start of Combat) is the tribe's best hidden depth; keep it and show the order in the UI.

standouts.why: Master of the Cork-Pop doubles the Hen, Hartmut's chain and Altmark's trophies at once, a multiplier that rewards building the Duel web.
Dame Reisig crowns another tribe's carry, so a huge Ooze or a returning Bird soaks every Knight buff: the off-label use Johnny wants.
The Chronicler forces a buy-to-cross-out rhythm against the empty-slot cards, and crossing out a full Ooze spills its Belly onto the board.

weakest.why: Grit-Pit Forager is a plain Proud stat drip with no second use.
Sprucehold Envoy is a generic Discover with a small-board bonus.
Pennon-Squire's +1/+1 and Duel is thin and does one job.

flags.note: Clashes with the Champion keyword on whether Hens can be Champion.
Sir Gottfried at x4 (x7 golden) on a fed Champion, stacked with Herald's Duels, could end fights before they start.
Sir Altmark with Herald and Cork-Pop takes up to six quarter-trophies a fight, all permanent.
Refectory Prior golden pays 4 gold a turn on a three-unit board, which this tribe plays by design.
